slot.brief: From percentage composition of C, H and O, determine empirical formula and then molecular formula from molar mass.

stem: An organic compound contains $53.3\%$ carbon, $11.1\%$ hydrogen, and $35.6\%$ oxygen by mass. If its molar mass is $90\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$, its molecular formula is:

verdicts.working: Mole ratio C:H:O = 53.3/12 : 11.1/1 : 35.6/16 = 4.44 : 11.1 : 2.225 ≈ 2:5:1, so empirical formula C2H5O (mass 45). n = 90/45 = 2 → molecular formula C4H10O2. Check: C 48/90=53.3%, H 10/90=11.1%, O 32/90=35.6% — matches.

working:
1. Find relative moles of each element in a $100\ \text{g}$ sample: $n_{\text{C}} = \dfrac{53.3}{12} = 4.44$, $n_{\text{H}} = \dfrac{11.1}{1} = 11.1$, $n_{\text{O}} = \dfrac{35.6}{16} = 2.225$. 2. Divide each by the smallest number of moles ($2.225$): $\text{C} = \dfrac{4.44}{2.225} = 2$, $\text{H} = \dfrac{11.1}{2.225} = 5$, $\text{O} = \dfrac{2.225}{2.225} = 1$. The empirical formula is $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{O}$. 3. Empirical formula mass $= 2(12) + 5(1) + 16 = 45\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$. 4. Multiplying factor $n = \dfrac{\text{Molar mass}}{\text{Empirical mass}} = \dfrac{90}{45} = 2$. 5. Molecular formula $= (\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{O})_2 = \text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}_2$.

Independent check: Mole ratio C:H:O = 53.3/12 : 11.1/1 : 35.6/16 = 4.44 : 11.1 : 2.225 ≈ 2:5:1, so empirical formula C2H5O (mass 45). n = 90/45 = 2 → molecular formula C4H10O2. Check: C 48/90=53.3%, H 10/90=11.1%, O 32/90=35.6% — matches.

Option C: Has the correct molar mass of $90\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$ but assumes a 1:2:1 ratio (lactic acid) instead of calculating from percentages.
